page: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g is a general-purpose cloud instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute line, positioned for modest computing workloads that benefit from dedicated core execution. The server provides two vCPUs derived from a single physical AMD EPYC core running at 2.0 GHz with two threads per core. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. It also supports modern instruction set extensions including AVX-512, SHA-NI, and AES encryption. Memory provisioning is set at 8.0 GB, establishing an even 4.0 GB per core balance. Attached storage consists of a minimal 1 GB local NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No hardware GPU acceleration is included.

Benchmark profiles show sharp contrasts between single-threaded efficiency and parallel capacity. In single-thread routines, the instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng evaluations as well as gzip compression reaching 39.96 GB/s and bzip3 decompression at 17.65 GB/s. Geekbench single-core scores reach 1820.0, placing it in the middle tier. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the limitations of a single physical core: stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores land in the lower quartiles. PassMark database operations and multi-threaded rendering tasks similarly place in the lowest tier, while Redis set throughput clocks at 3.96 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput holds steady at 8.04 GB/s, while small-model LLM generation reaches an average 106.45 tokens per second.

From a resource and infrastructure perspective, the vx1-g-2c-8g offers dependable, non-throttled compute capacity for tasks where multi-tenant contention must be avoided. The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides adequate headroom for general execution environments, though the 1 GB local storage footprint strictly limits onboard persistent data without external network storage. This configuration functions effectively for single-threaded data transformation, lightweight continuous integration workers, proxy layers, static web servers, and low-traffic API backends that do not require substantial disk capacity or heavy multi-core database concurrency.
description: Vultr vx1-g-2c-8g is a general-purpose cloud compute instance designed for entry-level server workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers two vCPUs mapped to a single physical core with two threads, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 vector support. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance, while local storage is restricted to a compact 1 GB NVMe SSD volume alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmark results demonstrate notable strength in single-threaded tasks, such as top-tier gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, alongside solid static web serving throughput of 8.04 GB/s. However, multi-core throughput and database operations show constrained capacity due to the dual-thread ceiling. The vx1-g-2c-8g represents a cost-effective, predictable configuration tailored for lightweight background workers, small-scale API endpoints, static web hosting, and routine automation scripts.
